proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus is a kind of legal power or entitlement — specifically the right to alienate, destroy, or fundamentally alter a thing — that inheres in a property-owning agent by virtue of their legally recognised status as dominus. It is externally grounded in the Roman-law property system (not in any intrinsic physical property of the bearer), making it a Role in BFO terms. It is best treated as a class (a kind of legal right) rather than an individual because it names a type of entitlement that any dominus may instantiate. Modelling it as a subclass of working:LegalRight (itself typed as BFO_0000023) preserves continuity with the existing ontology and correctly places it in the specifically-dependent-continuant branch.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a species of LegalRight (already typed as BFO_0000023 Role): every instance of Abusus is an instance of LegalRight, distinguished by its content (alienation/destruction of the res) within Roman-law property doctrine.

Inherited via the LegalRight parent, but stated explicitly to satisfy BFO typing requirements: Abusus is a Role — externally grounded in legal-institutional recognition, inhering in an agent qua dominus.

open_questions: Should Abusus be modelled as a class (a type of legal right any dominus can bear) or as a named individual representing the abstract Roman-law concept as a specific GDC information artefact? The current proposal treats it as a class.

Roman property theory also recognises Usus (use) and Fructus (enjoyment of fruits) alongside Abusus as the three sticks of dominium. Should we mint sibling classes Usus and Fructus now for completeness, perhaps under a common superclass working:Dominium or working:PropertyRight?
Is the bearer of Abusus always a natural person (BFO_0000040 individual) or can it inhere in a corporate/legal-person entity? This affects whether we need an additional bearer-type annotation.

Should working:LegalRight be further refined — e.g., does Abusus require a corresponding working:LegalObligation on third parties (a Hohfeldian correlative), and if so, should that relation be asserted here?
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus, the Roman-law right of abuse (ius abutendi), is the entitlement of a dominus to alienate, consume, or destroy the res. Ontologically it is an externally grounded entitlement that inheres in an agent solely by virtue of their legal status as property owner within a recognised legal system — the hallmark of a BFO Role (BFO_0000023). It is not a physical capacity of the owner (which would be a Disposition) nor a measurable property (Quality), but a socially/institutionally conferred normative power. Because Abusus names a kind of entitlement that any dominus may bear rather than one particular historical artefact, it is typed as a class, not an individual. It is placed as a subclass of the existing working:LegalRight class (already typed BFO_0000023), inheriting that typing and keeping the graph consistent. The specifically-dependent-continuant character is preserved: an instance of Abusus inheres in exactly one bearer at any time and is realised whenever that bearer exercises the right (e.g., in an act of alienation, a BFO_0000015 Process).
